matching.__comment_boostMode: Score on the decision rules alone; upstream's default is 'sum', which adds Elasticsearch's unbounded BM25 relevance so a candidate failing a required field can still auto-link. Thresholds in decisionRules.json are calibrated to this setting.
matching.__comment_autoMatchPatientWithHumanAdjud: Deliberately absent, which OpenCR reads as false: once a record carries the humanAdjudication tag (set by /resolve-match-issue when a flag is cleared, and by /break-match), automatic matching will never move its golden link again - new matches surface as conflicts for a person to look at. Setting it true lets automation overrule that, including a deliberate break-match, which is the false merge this whole ruleset is shaped to avoid. Not exposed in mediator.json's configDefs on purpose: it must not become a one-click toggle in the OpenHIM console. Note that the OpenHIM push replaces this whole matching struct at runtime, so a value set only here would be dropped anyway - false and absent behave identically, so this stays a comment rather than a key.

internalid.__comment_displayname: internalid is the per-record registration handle; for SEDISH that is the source-key (present on 100% of records). 5-code-national and 6-biometrics were removed from this list so CRUX labels them via their own blocks (National ID / National FP ID) instead of all showing as 'Internal ID'. The decision rules match by fhirpath/system, so this display-only split does not affect matching.

codest.__comment: 6-code-st is the system our sites actually emit; the pre-existing 4-code-st matches no record. Display-only: adding a per-facility id here (never to internalid, whose uris are upsert handles) cannot fuse patients across sites.

biometricnational.__comment: Every iSantePlus deployment host for the biometric code, mirroring nationalid above. Display only; matching is driven by the fhirpath in decisionRules.json and the espath in PatientRelationship.json, which carry the same list and must be kept in step with it.

__comments.matching.tool: this tells if the app should use mediator algorithms or elasticsearch algorithms for matching, two options mediator and elasticsearch
